reason: The text depicts multiple non-leader figures exercising agency. Rebekah (a wife, not a formal leader) takes independent initiative to inquire of the Lord when distressed about her pregnancy (וַתֵּלֶךְ לִדְרֹשׁ אֶת־ יְהוָה). Jacob (the younger, non-primary son) deliberately cooks stew and initiates a negotiation with Esau to trade for his birthright. Esau makes his own decisions regarding his inheritance. While Isaac (the patriarch/leader) also shows agency through prayer, the narrative clearly grants agency to multiple subordinate characters, including a woman and younger sons, thereby contradicting the exclusivist claim.
